articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 39: Prosecution drops 3 charges, to focus on unexplained wealth
articles.summary: The 39th day of Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial was supposed to focus on scheduling the remaining proceedings. Instead, the prosecution made a major move, asking the Senate…

blocks.text: The 39th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial was supposed to focus on scheduling the remaining proceedings. Instead, the prosecution made a major move, asking the Senate impeachment court to allow it to drop three of the four impeachment articles and focus on Article 2.

The article accuses Duterte of amassing unexplained wealth by failing to declare assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) and divest business interests as required by the Constitution.

The prosecution moved to drop Article 1 on confidential fund misuse, Article 3 on bribery, and Article 4 on alleged threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family. The move followed a week of testimony from financial regulators, bank and insurance officials, tax authorities, and lawyer-accountant Alexander Cabrera, who helped establish allegations that Duterte and her husband allegedly amassed at least P817 million and as much as P1.5 billion in unexplained wealth.

The motion by the prosecutors was granted by the Senate impeachment court, saying that such a decision has a precedent: the 2012 impeachment trial of then Chief Justice Renato Corona. Then, prosecutors were allowed to drop five out of the eight Articles of Impeachment after presenting evidence on three Articles.

House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro of Batangas said the move was made for exigency in response to the public, who has long been awaiting a verdict on an impeachment case that took two years before reaching the trial stage. She also stressed that the Senate is in the thick of deliberating the proposed P7.2 trillion budget for 2027.

“The rest have been withdrawn already, but only for the interest of the public, for the interest of the Senate as the institution. We are willing to take that position that we are all in here in Article 2 on unexplained wealth,” Luistro said in a press conference.

“We believe we have presented sufficient evidence that warrants the removal from office for culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust. Let us give justice to the Filipino people who have been waiting for this conclusion,” she added.
Senator-judge Alan Cayetano and defense counsel Sheila Sison, however, disagreed.

Cayetano said the impeachment has no timeline, while Sison said that the prosecution cannot be allowed to have the benefit of its accusations without bearing the burden of having those accusations tested.

"In other words, the prosecution would thus retain the benefit of having its evidence heard, while the respondent would be at risk of being denied the benefit of having that evidence contradicted,” she added.

To this, private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said, “They always play the victim card. Wait a minute. Hindi siya ang victim, ang taong bayan ang victim dito. Who is being unfair here? Who is being unjust? The Vice President herself. She refuses to come and defend herself in the impeachment court. And yet she does press conferences saying this trial is a farce. If that is their style, then they come to court with unclean hands."

“They cannot say they were deprived of presenting countervailing facts. They cross-examined all our witnesses for hours, for days. The defense cannot say they were not given a fair shake,” private prosecutor Amado Ligutan added.
After allowing the dropping of the three Articles of Impeachment, presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero lifted the sub judice, or the gag order on parties concerning Articles 1, 3 and 4.

Escudero, however, clarified that the court’s ruling on the prosecution’s dropping of three charges and the lifting of the sub judice rule for the withdrawn allegations is subject to appeal by the senator-judges once the parties have had time to reflect on the matter.
Escudero announced the November schedule of the impeachment trial days.
November 9: Court will convene at 10 a.m.; the Senate will have a session in the afternoon and resume the trial after the session
November 10: Whole day, from 10 a.m. onwards
November 11: Court will convene at 10 a.m.; the Senate may conduct a session in the afternoon as needed
November 12: Whole day, from 10 a.m. onwards
November 13: Whole day, from 10 a.m. onwards
November 19: Whole day, from 10 a.m. onwards
November 20: Whole day, from 10 a.m. onwards
November 23: From 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. only
—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Kelly Clarkson is feuding with a Brooklyn store over alleged 'Pretty Woman' treatment
articles.summary: Kelly Clarkson has spent the weekend trading verbal blows with a curiosity shop in Brooklyn, N.Y., after she claimed they gave her a Pretty Woman-style brush-off when she inquired about the price of…

image.caption: Kelly Clarkson performs on NBC's Today show at Rockefeller Plaza on Tuesday, May 6, 2025, in New York. (Charles Sykes/Invision/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Kelly Clarkson has spent the weekend trading verbal blows with a curiosity shop in Brooklyn, N.Y., after she claimed they gave her a Pretty Woman-style brush-off when she inquired about the price of a specialty item — an item that the shop says was never for sale in the first place.
A yellow wooden bird with a $15,000 US price tag next to it is at the centre of the spat

Kelly Clarkson has spent the weekend trading verbal blows with a curiosity shop in Brooklyn after she claimed they gave her a Pretty Woman-style brush-off when she inquired about the price of a specialty item — an item that the shop says was never for sale in the first place.
The online feud started on Saturday, when the singer posted that she had driven to the New York borough of Brooklyn to "check out this store I thought looked really rad."
Clarkson said she was planning to buy "a few things," but "literally was looked at as if I couldn't afford it," writing she was told by a worker that "he could find something comparable for me."

"But y'all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts' character in Pretty Woman," she concluded, referencing a scene in the 1990 rom-com in which Roberts' character is treated rudely by a snooty saleswoman in an upscale boutique.
Art of Play sells a mixture of home goods, puzzles, games and toys, and also hosts a small theatre that runs magic shows.

Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me. Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale. But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman. For sure, check it out 👎—kellyclarkson
The store responded Sunday, stating that Clarkson had asked about buying "Molly," a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton" which "is permanently attached to the wall and isn't for sale."
They noted that Clarkson's version of events "would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged," but said that all patrons at Art of Play "are equally welcome."
"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by eight million people who have never visited our store," the shop wrote on Instagram.
For sale or not?
Clarkson hit back later that day, posting a photo showing a $15,000 US price tag on the wall next to the wooden bird automaton in question.
"So you're not only rude, you're also a liar. [...] It's not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you, my friend, were an exception."
Kelly Clarkson arrives at the 51st Daytime Emmy Awards in Los Angeles on June 7, 2024. (Jordan Strauss/Invision/The Associated Press)

Clarkson rarely makes personal posts on social media. Prior to Saturday's post, her most recent post on X was a promotional post two weeks prior for Season 30 of The Voice, in which Clarkson appears as a coach.

The shop then stated Monday that they had told Clarkson that the artist behind the automaton had a "nearly identical" copy he could sell her for $15,000 US, adding that they also offered to show her a different bird automaton for sale in the shop.
"It costs about $2,000. She did not stick around long enough to see it."

items: Hudson Williams wore this cardigan. Then the Indigenous designer's business went viral
North of North embodies the slow fashion trend with practical works of art in Season 2

blocks.text: Several commenters on Art of Play's initial post backed up Clarkson's account about the price tag, with makeup artist and influencer Joey Camasta stating the price tag was there when he visited in August.

Other comments defended the shop, suggesting an earlier Sept. 5 post by Art of Play about no-cost experiences available at the shop, which included a photo of Molly, implied the automaton was always an exception — price tag notwithstanding.

The tiff has sparked mixed reactions online, with some criticizing the singer for bringing her fame and fandom down on a small business, and others slamming the shop's response as unprofessional and noting that regardless of whether the bird was for sale or not, everyone deserves to feel respected when entering a business.
CBC News has reached out to Clarkson's team and Art of Play for comment.
The bird at the centre
So who is Molly?
The automaton is a bright yellow, wall-mounted wooden bird. When a crank is operated, the bird darts about with surprisingly life-like precision, emitting bird song.

It's the creation of Seattle-based artist Bliss Kolb, whose website features a number of wooden automatons, including several other birds, as well as butterflies and a dragonfly, ranging in price from $4,000 to $12,000 US.

A 2025 Instagram post by 69 Atlantic, which runs the magic shows at Art of Play, notes that Molly sings the opening for each weekend show and says there is a "Do Not Touch" sign nearby, as she is delicate.
"Aside from the controversy, it's refreshing that this non-computer ‘entertainment' can inspire joy and fascination … no screen," one commenter noted on Tuesday.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Alexandra Mae Jones is a senior writer for CBC News based in Toronto. She has written on a variety of topics, from health to pop culture to breaking news, and previously reported for CTV News and the Toronto Star. She joined CBC in 2024. You can reach her at alexandra.mae.jones@cbc.ca

articles.title: Pope admitted to hospital for surgery to remove lump on his lung
articles.summary: Pope Leo has said the growth is "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage".

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome's Gemelli Hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung, detected during what the Vatican has described as "routine checks".
It said the operation would take place on Tuesday afternoon.
The 71-year-old pontiff was met at the hospital by a large crowd, some of whom had been waiting outside for several hours to catch a glimpse of him.
They cheered greetings and well wishes as he passed, waving and smiling back through the lowered back window of his car.
He was then met by staff on the hospital steps. "I'm sorry," one of them commiserated, to which the Pope gave a smile and a shrug. "We're here for you," he was assured.
It was Leo XIV himself who on Sunday announced news of his operation to the world, speaking from the balcony in St Peter's Square after delivering the traditional Angelus blessing.
He said the nodule, or growth, on his lung was "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage", but that doctors had advised him to have it removed.
The Vatican said the Pope would be operated on by the Gemelli's thoracic surgery team and promised an update on his condition on Tuesday evening.
His schedule has already been cleared until 20 October to give him time to recover.
Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous. But doctors say when a lump is removed it will usually be tested to check for any sign of the disease.
The Vatican has stressed that the pontiff, who is generally thought to be fit, had no symptoms of infection or illness.
Cardinal Kikuchi Tarcisio Isao of Tokyo wrote on social media that he'd had an audience with Pope Leo on Monday, and said the pontiff felt "nothing wrong" physically.
He said the Pope had decided to check in for surgery as soon as possible because he was due to travel to Latin America in early November, and was keen to stick to that plan.
The trip is particularly significant because it includes a visit to Peru, where the pontiff was a missionary and then a Bishop for many years.
Despite all the reassurances, the news has shaken Catholics all over the world.
"Am I worried? Yes, because I certainly wasn't expecting anything like this," Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Parolin told journalists on Tuesday.
He agreed that the news was like a "bolt from the blue", but said the cardinals had been struck by the Pope's "serenity" and were confident in his recovery.
Outside Gemelli Hospital, which has treated several popes and is home to a large statue of John Paul II, a few Catholics lingered after the pontiff was admitted.
Carla had come specially, wanting to be close.
"He seems calm, so we are calm too - even though illness is always unpleasant," she told the BBC. "We will wait here and pray."

"I was in St Peter's Square when he made the announcement, and I felt really awful," said Elsa, who was also present. "I was really taken aback," she said, explaining that when Pope Leo was elected she had thought he was a younger, healthier pontiff.
"It turns out he's vulnerable too. I really hope it's something superficial, that can be contained, like he told us."

articles.title: How will emergency rule in Pakistan's northwest affect Afghan ties?
articles.summary: Pakistan's decision to suspend Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's provincial government could further strain already tense relations between Islamabad and Kabul.

image.caption: Islamabad blames Afghan-based elements for launching militant attacks on PakistanImage: Anjum Naveed/AP/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pakistan on Sunday announced that the northwestern province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa had been put under emergency rule.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's federal government defended the move, saying the provincial administration — led by imprisoned former Prime Minister Imran Khan's Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party — was working "hand in glove" with the Pakistani Taliban, known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

"The PTI government in the province has not equipped the police and security forces to counter militancy. Instead, they have links with TTP and did not cooperate with the federal government to fight terrorism," Talal Chaudhry, minister of state for interior affairs, told DW.
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the government had "solid evidence" to support its allegations, the Associated Press news agency reported.
He said the suspension and imposition of a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would allow security forces and the new administration to better coordinate efforts to combat terrorism.
The move comes as thousands of Khan supporters continue to stage anti-government protests and demand the former leader be released from jail.
But the federal government has denied that its action was driven by domestic politics.
Are Pakistan and Afghanistan heading for war?
A stronghold of Imran Khan's PTI
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which has suffered an increasing number of militant attacks in recent months, is a political stronghold of former PM Khan.
The cricketer-turned-politician has been in jail since 2023 on corruption and other charges that he and his supporters say are politically motivated.
His PTI party had long governed the volatile province, but Islamabad's decision to impose emergency rule has now effectively removed it from power.
Pakistan's constitution ​allows the federal government to take over from provincial authorities during an emergency.

Islamabad said Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would now be administered directly by a new governor, assisted by an advisory council. This arrangement will initially be in place for six months, but could be extended for as long as necessary, authorities said.
Is governor rule the solution?
Khan's party has lambasted the suspension of the provincial government.
"This is more a coup disguised as emergency and governor rule," said PTI spokesperson Sayed Zulfikar Bukhari.

It has also sparked questions about provincial autonomy and the future of civilian rule, with critics warning that the abrupt removal of an elected administration risks weakening accountability and deepening political divisions.

"Governor's rule should only be imposed in extreme constitutional crises, not political disputes, and its legality should be reviewed by the Constitutional Court," Osama Malik, a senior constitutional expert, told DW.
"While it may temporarily reduce militant attacks, lasting security requires political engagement and stronger civilian law enforcement."
Why Pakistan is fighting the Taliban it once backed
Raja Qaiser Ahmed, assistant professor of regional security and foreign affairs at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad, echoed this view.
"Federal rule can never be a substitute for an elected political authority. The argument of provincial autonomy would also definitely surface amidst this uncharacteristic measure taken," he told DW.
"It may, though, streamline coordination between the federal government and the province, which was a missing link for quite some time."
Surging militancy poses acute security challenges
Pakistan has seen a surge in militant violence in recent years.
Authorities have recorded more than 2,800 militant attacks since January, which have killed or wounded about 3,000 people, according to the AP news agency.
Islamabad blames Afghan-based elements for the attacks and has accused the ruling Taliban of allowing Afghan territory to be used to harbor militants.

Pakistan wants Kabul to clamp down on the TTP, which is a separate group but closely linked to the Afghan Taliban. The TTP seeks to impose a hard-line interpretation of Islam, particularly in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

"We have been asking Kabul to recognize terrorists as terrorists and take action against them. They must do so because their own peace, security, and future are linked to Pakistan," asserted Chaudhry, the deputy interior minister.
The Afghan Taliban deny the allegations and say they cannot be held accountable for security incidents inside Pakistan.
How 5 years of Taliban rule have changed Afghanistan
Will it escalate the Afghanistan-Pakistan conflict?
The dispute has fueled growing tensions between the neighbors, which have escalated into armed clashes in recent months, heightening fears of a wider confrontation.
Ahmed believes the suspension of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's provincial government is likely to aggravate tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
"Security measures taken in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa would further impinge on the Pakistan-Afghan relationship, which is seemingly locked in a protracted cycle of offense and escalation," said Ahmed.
After announcing emergency rule, Islamabad also authorized the deployment of additional army troops and military equipment to the region to support authorities.

Ayesha Siddiqa, an independent military and security analyst, warned that the suspension of the elected provincial government could complicate counterterrorism efforts by deepening resentment among local communities.

"After ending the political government, I don't think the security situation will improve. In fact, there will be less willingness among local communities to support counterterrorism operations," she told DW.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia's military struggle against Houthi attacks
articles.summary: Houthi attacks on airports and energy facilities are putting Saudi Arabia under pressure. Could a Saudi-led international military offensive succeed against the Iran-aligned Houthi militia in Yemen?

image.caption: The Houthis held a recruitment drive in Sanaa, Yemen on October 7Image: Mohammed Huwais/AFP

blocks.text: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi militia continues to escalate its attacks on Saudi Arabia targeting energy facilities but, above all, airports.
On Saturday, a missile attack on Riyadh's international airport killed 13 people and injured more than 300. In a second attack on Sunday, the militia killed another civilian and injured 11 others.

According to their own statements, the Houthis also attacked Saudi Arabia's airport in Dammam and two oil facilities within the past 24 hours. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud warned of the consequences for energy security and announced a strong response.

According to a report by the US think tank American Enterprise Institute, Saudi Arabia is targeting Houthi missile launch pads, storage facilities and other military infrastructure in Yemen. The institute quotes Saudi military spokesman Turki al-Maliki in its October 11 report as saying that 136 military targets have already been destroyed.

However, years of Saudi-led military intervention between 2015 and 2022 in Yemen have not succeeded in defeating the Houthi militia. Moreover, the Saudi-led international coalition formed in 2015 has fallen apart and the United Arab Emirates has withdrawn its troops.

The Iran-aligned Houthis not only control large parts of northern Yemen but also increasingly the western coastline from where they disrupt international shipping through the Red Sea and the strategically important Bab el-Mandeb Strait. In early September, drones also severely damaged the Saudi East-West oil pipeline. The temporary shutdown disrupted oil exports and increased risks for the energy markets.
Why can't the Saudis defeat the Houthis?
Saudi Arabia calls on Pakistan, Turkey, the United States

For weeks, the Saudi government has been seeking allies in the fight against the Houthi militia. In late September, the United Kingdom and France pledged military support to defend Saudi infrastructure. London offered aerial refueling for Saudi fighter jets, while Paris announced it would provide troops, radar systems and air defense technology to protect the Yanbu oil terminal.

However, while the US recently refused to fight alongside Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, there could now be a change of heart in Washington, writes political analyst Osamah Al-Rawhani in a study by the Yemeni think tank Sanaa Center for Strategic Studies.

He notes that it remains to be seen whether this could actually lead to a successful offensive, as holding on to captured territories and launching counterattacks require significant financial resources, political commitment and the necessary resolve.

In his view, it is questionable whether Saudi Arabia would be able to muster the necessary perseverance. The kingdom could, however, change its current strategy. "If the costs of the war continue to rise, Riyadh might look for a way to withdraw from the conflict," Al-Rawhani says.

blocks.caption: Observers note that Saudi Arabia is facing an asymmetrical war as the Houthis don't need to win militarily for disrupting Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 and oil exports Image: Osamah Abdulrahman/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Saudi Arabia's asymmetrical war against the Houthis
Marcus Schneider, project manager at the Friedrich Ebert Foundation's Center of Expertise on Peace and Security in the Middle East and North Africa, shares a similar view.

"To eliminate the Houthis, ground troops would be needed but Riyadh has no experience with this type of warfare, especially in a foreign country," Schneider recently told DW. As such, he believes the Saudi leadership is less concerned with achieving a military victory than with reducing its vulnerability, securing the broadest possible coalition of partners and gaining political maneuvering room.

"The Houthis are well-entrenched in Yemen and can withstand considerable blows. Above all, Saudi Arabia needs stability for its Vision 2030 reform set and that is currently further away than ever," Schneider said.

He added that military asymmetry is also a key factor: Saudi Arabia possesses modern weapons and spends enormous sums on its armed forces. The Houthis, on the other hand, do not need to win a conventional war. It is enough for them to deploy missiles and drones, threaten infrastructure and disrupt shipping traffic.

blocks.caption: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (C) is hoping for military support by his defense allies Pakistan and Turkey Image: Turkish Presidency/UPI Photo/newscom/picture alliance

blocks.text: Are the UAE, Pakistan, Turkey changing course?

Saudi Arabia may also be able to turn to another partner in the region: the United Arab Emirates (UAE). According to media reports, Anwar Gargash, a senior diplomatic advisor to the UAE president, spoke out in favor of closer security cooperation among the Gulf states. "We are all targets," he stated on X.

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have undermined the security of the entire region, he notes. "It is necessary to revitalize cooperation among the Gulf states, particularly in the areas of security and defense, and to strengthen the collective security system," Gargash added.
Pakistan, which signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement in early August along with Saudi Arabia and Turkey, also initially ruled out military intervention.

According to media reports, however, the country is now said to be carrying out airstrikes on Houthi missile and drone positions — a claim that Islamabad denies. Pakistan does not intend to deploy ground troops. Turkey, another member of the Mecca Pact, rules out an offensive military operation but is providing air defense equipment.

Saudi Arabia can thus build on additional military support, according to an analysis by the US think tank Soufan Center. Whether this will result in an effective strategy, however, depends on whether the partners go beyond limited airstrikes and political expressions of solidarity and on whether the fragmented Yemeni government forces can better coordinate their military operations.

Meanwhile, Iran has offered to act as a mediator between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis. However, given Iran's support for the Houthis and the recent attacks on Saudi Arabia, it is questionable whether Saudi Arabia will accept this offer.

Saudi Arabia and the US are allies, whereas Iran and the US have been at war since February. It is also unclear whether Tehran wields sufficient influence over the Yemeni militia to persuade it to halt the attacks.
Saudi Arabia on the backfoot in the war against the Houthis
This article was originally published in German.

articles.title: Kimberly Guilfoye : US ambassador to Greece resigns amid misconduct allegations
articles.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle has resigned as US ambassador to Greece. President Trump previously said he was unhappy with her amid reports of a bribery scandal and ethics violations.

image.caption: Kimberly Guilfoyle has been plagued by allegations of misconduct including attempted influence peddling and briberyImage: Nicolas Koutsokostas/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Kimberly Guilfoyle has stepped down as US ambassador to Greece.
White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia earlier told reporters that Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, calling her "an incredible asset to the team."
Zacharia, continued by adding, "we wish her well," though did not say whether she had already stepped down.

Guilfoyle's position became untenable after the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported on her supposed threats against Greece and her acceptance of improper gifts. Most recently, WSJ published an article with screenshots of text messages documenting her attempts to receive cash from a Republican donor in exchange for influence in the Trump administration.
Trump before firing: 'We're not happy'

The past week has seen much speculation as to whether Guilfolyle would have to go, with the Associated Press (AP) revealing that President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio were "extremely pissed off" over the former Fox News host's conduct.
On Monday, Trump said "we're looking at it" when asked if Guilfoyle could be fired, adding, "we're not happy."
Rubio initially defended Guilfoyle and continued to do so in Greece last week, saying, "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here."

Ultimately, however, he lashed out at journalists for asking about the allegations against Guilfoyle, accusing them of seeing their own reporting as "gospel" and insisting that he would not comment until he knew the whole story.
Guilfoyle has yet to address the accusations, though on Sunday her lawyers said that she had done nothing wrong.
There have been mixed reports suggesting that the State Department's investigator general might look into the matter, though this has not yet been confirmed.
Top Democrats in the House of Representatives and the Senate have called for investigations.

blocks.caption: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was reportedly 'extremely pissed off' at Guilfoyle over embarrassing allegations tied to accusations of attempted influence peddlingImage: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What exactly is Guilfoyle accused of?

Guilfoyle, a TV personality who was formerly married to California Governor Gavin Newsom and later engaged to Trump's eldest son Don Jr., has been accused of numerous improprieties during her tenure in Greece.
Greece is an important NATO ally for the US, especially in the Eastern Mediterranean and in terms of Red Sea shipping security.

Among other things, she is said to have bragged about luxury travel and the perks of chumming with energy company executives before threatening that the US could easily undermine Greek democracy if it did not get what it wanted from the host country.
She also appeared to favor shady deals with individual Greek construction and energy company execs, going so far as to bring their lobbyists to top-level diplomatic meetings.

Guilfoyle was further reported to have alienated embassy staffer with her behavior and reportedly exploded after not being invited to a Greek-themed event at this year's World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, demanding she be allowed to attend.

The straw that broke the camel's back, however, was a media offensive started by GOP donor Eric Deters, who grew weary of Guilfoyle's insistence that he pay off her in exchange for influence that she had been unable to deliver.

Deters began doing media interviews with any outlet that would listen after the WSJ story broke, publishing embarrassing text chains in which Guilfoyle implored him to transfer $100,000 (€89, 400) to her American Express card, writing, "Honey please, I need you to get this done for me today."

Deters, who said he had already paid her $300,000 and had gotten nothing in return, told numerous US media outlets the deal was "absolutely a quid pro quo" and that he had warned Guilfoyle that he would go public about their dealings if she could not rectify the situation.

articles.title: More Pinoys paying for premium chat services
articles.summary: ilipinos are spending more to access premium services on chat apps, particularly Viber, whose paid subscription segment grew by more than a third this year.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am

Rakuten Viber senior director for Asia Pacific David Tse said yesterday the messaging platform’s monthly active users in the Philippines increased by 17 percent this year, while its premium service Viber Plus grew at a faster pace of 34 percent.
Rakuten Viber
MANILA, Philippines — Filipinos are spending more to access premium services on chat apps, particularly Viber, whose paid subscription segment grew by more than a third this year.

Viber Plus costs P99 a month and allows users to edit and delete messages without a trace. The subscription also removes advertisements from the app and offers an invisible mode that lets users hide their online status while still seeing whether others are active.
Beyond messaging, Viber recorded a 97 percent increase in users on its dating service and a 21 percent rise in businesses on its enterprise channel.
The company is preparing to enter into a new partnership with the Department of Tourism to bring more tourism operators, including hotels and restaurants, onto the platform.
Rakuten Viber estimates that 41 percent of the Philippine population uses the app for work-related chats.
Professionals favor the platform for its end-to-end encryption, which protects messages and data exchanged between senders and recipients from access by third parties, including Rakuten Viber itself.

articles.title: Gatchalian thanks Sotto for ‘proper’ office turnover
articles.summary: Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday thanked his predecessor, now-Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III, for turning over the office of the chamber’s highest official in tip…

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian.
STAR / Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian yesterday thanked his predecessor, now-Senate President Pro Tempore Vicente Sotto III, for turning over the office of the chamber’s highest official in tip top shape.
Contributed photos of the office showed that Sotto turned over the Senate President’s office to Gatchalian with the polished wooden floors, granite countertops and sofas intact and in place.
Gatchalian thanked Sotto for giving him his personal chair and sofa, saying the leadership is ready to buckle down to work.
“It’s beautiful. I am thankful to Sen. Sotto because he even left me his personal chair and sofa,” Gatchalian said.
“So, I am ready to move in, hit the ground running because I will no longer worry about the renovation,” he added.

Sotto’s turnover was a direct contrast to what flood control suspect and suspended senator Jinggoy Estrada did to the Senate President Pro Tempore office, which was stripped of all fixtures and defaced.
Estrada justified his move saying turning over an office in that condition is “standard practice.”
Gatchalian disagreed, saying “respect and courtesy should be the standard.”

Sotto served as Senate President from September 2025 to May 2026. He was ousted from the post by Alan Peter Cayetano in May. Cayetano only lasted a month before his ouster by Gatchalian. Sotto was elected Gatchalian’s Pro Tempore.
Meanwhile, Estrada served as Senate President Pro Tempore during the May 2024-September 2025 Senate presidency of Francis Escudero.
Case vs Sotto junked

In a related development, the Supreme Court threw out the petition for indirect contempt against Sotto over his opposition to a previous ruling that nullified the articles of impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte in 2025.

The high tribunal unanimously dismissed the petition for indirect contempt against Sotto filed by a group composed of lawyers Manuelito Luna, Ferdinand Topacio and Reina Mercedes, Isabela Vice Mayor Harold Respicio, retired brigadier general Virgilio Garcia and Mary Catherine Diaz Binag in February this year.

In a statement yesterday, the SC declared “Sotto’s disagreement with the impeachment ruling and its ponente, Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, was part of public debate on an issue of national importance.”

In absolving Sotto, the SC said his pronouncements did not pass what it called the “incitement test” and the “clear and present danger test” that both assess the likelihood of carrying violence as a result of related speech.
The high court emphasized that “provocative, harsh or critical statements are still protected speech.”
In a statement, Sotto clarified that his previous disagreement with the ruling did not equate to a lack of respect for the judiciary.

“I disagreed with one of its decisions. That does not mean I have lost respect for the Court. I have always held it in high regard as an institution, and I return the respect it has shown me in its decision,” he said. – Ghio Ong, Neil Jayson Servallos

articles.title: AFP backs Gibo on cutting comms with China military
articles.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines has expressed full support for Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr.’s decision to cut military-to-military communications with China.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa
MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines has expressed full support for Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro Jr.’s decision to cut military-to-military communications with China.

The AFP made its position known in response to the Chinese embassy’s statement Monday night criticizing how Teodoro “decided to shut down” military-to-military communication between China and the Philippines “for political self interests.”

AFP spokesman for the West Philippine Sea, retired rear admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, said the military “stands solidly behind and firmly support the statement or the action of the (Secretary of National Defense) to suspend direct communication channels with the People’s Republic of China.”

“For communication mechanisms to work they have to be anchored on mutual trust, sincerity and support for international law. Bilateral dialogue will be effective if the messages matched the actions on sea, air and ground. Unfortunately this has not been the case,” he said.

“The direct communications has been used as a smokescreen by the Chinese Communist Party to perpetuate their illegal presence, coercive and aggressive actions and deceptive messaging not only on our maritime domain but even on land,” Trinidad said.
“Hence, the AFP fully supports and stands with the action of the (Secretary of National Defense) to suspend direct communication channels with the People’s Republic of China,” he added.
Trinidad declared that the AFP will continue to perform its mandate of patrolling the seas and “will keep performing our RORE (rotation and resupply) missions.”

“BRP Sierra Madre will remain a commissioned vessel of the Philippine Navy on Ayungin Shoal,” he said, adding that “the Filipino people could be assured that the AFP will ensure that our flag remains flying high and proud over our maritime domain.”

Reacting to Teodoro’s declaration, Palace press officer Claire Castro said the Philippines remains committed to maintaining its diplomatic and economic relations with Beijing and has no intention of severing ties with the Asian power.

“Perhaps it would be best to ask Secretary Gibo for specific details regarding that matter. But we are definitely not closing the door on our relationship with China. That’s not what the President wants,” Castro said.

“There is no prohibition in dealing with China in relation to trade and investment. Alam naman natin iyan (We are aware of that). And we are also dealing with China in a very diplomatic manner,” she said.
Castro reiterated that the Marcos government continues to engage Beijing while protecting the country’s sovereignty and national interests in the West Philippine Sea.
“We continue to engage with China, as we hope to sustain our strong trade and investment relationship with the country,” the Palace press officer emphasized. – Helen Flores

articles.title: Sandigan suspends anew Estrada for 90 days
articles.summary: The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has ordered another 90-day preventive suspension against Sen. Jinggoy Estrada.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am

Sen. Jinggoy Estrada, along with three of his co-accused, arrived at the Sandiganbayan in Quezon City on June 4, 2026 for the arraignment of their plunder case in connection with the alleged P573 million in illicit payouts from flood control projects.
The Philippine STAR / Miguel De Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has ordered another 90-day preventive suspension against Sen. Jinggoy Estrada.
In a five-page resolution penned by Associate Justice Zaldy Trespeses, Estrada is suspended from his Senate seat and any other public post he holds.
Estrada, who has been detained at the New Quezon City Jail since June 1, is accused of plunder over P573 million worth of alleged kickbacks from flood control projects.
His suspension issued in June by the anti-graft court’s Second Division expired.
The court asked the Senate President to implement the suspension and report back within five days of receipt.
Meanwhile, for lack of merit, the removal of former public works secretary Manuel Bonoan as an accused in Estrada’s plunder and graft cases has been upheld by the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division.
The anti-graft court denied the motions for reconsideration filed by Estrada and three former public works engineers, who sought a reversal of the ruling excluding Bonoan as an accused.

articles.title: Meralco rates up this month
articles.summary: More than eight million customers of Manila Electric Co. should brace for higher power rates this month following an increase in generation charges.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
A Meralco lineman repairs an electrical line along Jupiter Street in Makati in this file photo from March.
Ryan Baldemor
MANILA, Philippines — More than eight million customers of Manila Electric Co. (Meralco) should brace for higher power rates this month following an increase in generation charges.

Meralco spokesman Joe Zaldarriaga reported at a media briefing yesterday an upward adjustment of P0.3191 per kilowatt-hour this month, bringing the overall rate for a typical household to P15.0615 per kWh.
For residential customers consuming 200 kWh, the rate hike translates to an additional P64 on their electricity bills.

The generation charge, which covers the cost of power Meralco procures from suppliers, rose by P0.4973 per kWh due to higher fuel costs and peso depreciation, which affected the cost of dollar-denominated supply deals.
The increase was partly offset by lower transmission charges from the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines (NGCP) and a net reduction in taxes and other charges.
Transmission charges fell by P0.1384 per kWh, mainly due to lower ancillary service costs, which cover backup capacity needed to maintain grid stability.
Taxes also declined by P0.1436 per kWh, reflecting a higher share of indigenous natural gas, which is exempt from value-added tax, and the removal of VAT on the system loss charge.
Meralco pays pass-through charges for generation and transmission to power producers and the NGCP, respectively, while taxes and other charges are remitted to the government.
The only portion that goes to Meralco is the distribution charge, which covers the delivery of electricity through its poles, wires and substations.
After more than 15 years, the Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has finally approved a new distribution rate for Meralco, whose vast franchise comprises Metro Manila and nearby provinces.
For the first regulatory period covering July 2026 to June 2030, the company’s average distribution rate will rise to P1.48 per kWh from the current P1.35 per kWh.
The regulator ordered Meralco to refund P2.64 billion over six months, equivalent to a reduction of P0.1733 per kWh for residential customers.
Neither the higher distribution rate nor the latest refund order has been reflected in Meralco’s electricity rates this month.
Although it has yet to receive copies of the two decisions, the country’s largest power utility said it is ready to implement the rate adjustments ordered by the regulator.

articles.title: ICC prosecutor wants more recorded testimonies
articles.summary: The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court has asked judges handling the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte to admit prior recorded testimonies of three…

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
Former president Rodrigo Duterte.
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecutor of the International Criminal Court (ICC) has asked judges handling the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte to admit prior recorded testimonies of three more witnesses in the case.

In a 14-page filing released on Monday, the ICC prosecutor formally asked the Trial Chamber III to admit the statements and associated materials relating to witnesses identified as P-1370, P-1393 and P-1416.

“As submitted, the prior recorded testimonies of the three witnesses do not concern the acts and conduct of the accused. They primarily relate to the contextual elements of crimes against humanity, particularly the policy to ‘neutralize’ through violent crimes, including murder, alleged criminals in the Philippines,” read the filing signed by ICC acting prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang.
“The prior recorded testimonies are therefore relevant, reliable, probative and suitable for formal submission in written form,” the filing added.
Rody attends hearing
Like last month’s pre-trial hearing, Duterte was again present during Tuesday’s status conference, seated at the back row of the defense section during the case’s fourth.
Duterte listened to the proceedings with headphones.
During the hearing, Presiding Judge Joanna Korner set the initial schedule for the trial, which is set to begin on Nov. 30.
The first week of the trial will be conducted with breaks every hour in consideration of Duterte’s health.
The hearings will be held from 10 a.m. to 11 a.m., 11:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., 1:30 p.m. to 2:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. to 4 p.m.

articles.title: ‘VP, husband had at least P1.5 billion unexplained wealth’
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio had unexplained wealth amounting to at least P1.5 billion based on voluminous bank, tax and other government records, an expert financial…

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
National Bureau of Investigation agents, led by NBI Director Mel- vin Matibag, carry boxes containing the bureau’s findings on the Duterte family, at the NBI office in Manila.
Mark Ernest Villeza

MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio had unexplained wealth amounting to at least P1.5 billion based on voluminous bank, tax and other government records, an expert financial forensic analyst revealed Monday.

Accountant-lawyer Alexander Cabrera made this estimate upon Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero’s query, as the prosecution presented its case on Article II or unexplained wealth.

“That is less than P1.6 billion, around P1.5 billion,” he told the court, adding that this was based on records and documents they have culled for three years, or from 2022 when Duterte was elected Vice President, until 2025, as per their verification.
The amount is nearly double the P817.87 million identified in Cabrera’s original forensic report.
Escudero asked Cabrera about his “ceiling” or “maximum” in terms of his assessment on all the records provided to him by public and private prosecutors.
The presiding officer also sought confirmation that the figure covered the four-year period without counting the same amounts twice.
“Yes. The amount per year differs. If you total it, that will be the ceiling,” Cabrera replied, referring to the P1.5 billion.
The expert witness likewise explained that his original findings were based on a conservative examination of financial records involving Duterte and her husband.

Cabrera cited P475 million in confidential funds that he had excluded, around P100 million in additional financial discrepancies and potentially higher amounts involving GenCorp Industries Inc., a company linked to the couple.

Escudero also examined how much of the original findings would remain if amounts attributed to three companies were excluded. He calculated that GenCorp accounted for P212.63 million, while Cale88 Foods Corp. and Metro City Chow Foods Corp. accounted for another P142.20 million.

Excluding all three companies would still leave P463.05 million in alleged unexplained wealth based on other financial records, including bank accounts and insurance policies – a computation Cabrera agreed with.
The expert also defended his decision to look beyond the companies’ separate legal identities, citing suspected tax fraud as the basis for attributing certain transactions to their shareholders.

He maintained that financial interests and amounts owed to Carpio should have been disclosed in the couple’s statements of assets, liabilities and net worth. However, Cabrera acknowledged that applicable liabilities, including unpaid taxes, would have to be deducted in determining the final amount.

articles.title: VP Sara: I will not resign, I will never resign
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte reiterated that she will not resign from her post amid the Senate impeachment trial and the various accusations being hurled against her.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — Vice President Sara Duterte reiterated that she will not resign from her post amid the Senate impeachment trial and the various accusations being hurled against her.

“No, no, no. I will not resign. I will never resign from the Office of the Vice President,” Duterte said yesterday in a chance interview during the Philippine Chamber of Commerce and Industry’s 52nd Philippine Business Conference and Expo at Manila Hotel.
Duterte also vowed to proceed with her presidential bid in 2028.

“Yes, yes. That’s why, in one way, I see it as a blessing, the impeachment trial, because that will allow people to examine and scrutinize their questions about my character. And I am grateful to the Philippine Chamber because since 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, until now they still invite me and they are still listening,” Duterte added.
Meanwhile, Duterte refused to answer if she and husband Manases Carpio have unexplained wealth.

“I won’t answer it because I want him (National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag) to call me first. Then he should lay it out well so I could answer his allegations properly,” Duterte said.

The NBI said it is zeroing in on several properties linked to Duterte and other family members after finding major discrepancies in the declared values in her statement of assets, liabilities and net worth (SALN) and the agency’s initial estimates.
Matibag said they have identified about 14 properties based on Duterte’s SALNs and conducted field inspections to compare the declarations with actual structures and improvements.
He said investigators found a property with a mansion, swimming pools and a helipad but which was declared as agricultural land.
A property declared with a value of P890,000 could actually carry a P61-million price tag, Matibag noted.
Defense mum
The defense team refused to confirm whether the Vice President will appear before the impeachment court after the House prosecution panel dropped its plan to call her as a hostile witness.
“Well, if I knew whether it would happen or not, I wouldn’t tell you, right? So, let’s just wait,” defense spokesman Michael Poa said.
Poa issued the reaction after private prosecutor Lorna Kapunan said having Duterte take the witness stand would only be an exercise in futility.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said Duterte’s impeachment trial will take a break starting today to give way to the deliberations for the P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 and will resume on Nov. 9 after Undas.
Then the defense starts presenting its counter-evidence on all three Articles of Impeachment.
Poa said there’s no sigh of relief on their part despite the decision of the House prosecution to drop the bribery charges against Duterte.
“I wish I could say that,” said Poa, adding that they are “a long way from finishing what we’re supposed to do and so we’re just focused on the task at hand, which is to present the defense.”
Witnesses ready
The defense has decided on the initial batch of witnesses it will present beginning on Nov. 9.
Poa, however, did not name the witnesses who are among the 90 individuals listed by Duterte’s legal panel.
“We have an idea of who our first few witnesses will be but of course we will not disclose that. We will manifest at the appropriate time,” Poa said.
Poa, however, said nothing is concrete.
“That will also depend on the availability of the witnesses,” said Poa, adding that the defense listed at least 30 trial days.
VP denies property
The Vice President denied owning the property which the NBI is looking at and criticized the use of public funds in going after her and her family members.

“It is alarming that the National Bureau of Investigation – an agency funded by the people – is utilizing its operations for activities that offer no clear public benefit. The lot shown in the photograph, which was claimed to be listed in my statement of assets, liabilities and net worth, does not belong to me,” Duterte said in a statement.

“This kind of public deception is the reason why the NBI was removed from the list of witnesses to be presented by the prosecution in the impeachment proceedings – stemming from allegations that they once again presented questionable evidence, much like the Gracioso affidavit,” Duterte added.
Attacks don’t work
The attacks against the Vice President are not working, as evidenced by the latest Pulse Asia survey where she remained the most preferred candidate for president.
Duterte’s spokesman Paolo Panelo noted that the various issues hurled against Duterte did not affect her rating.
“That’s why they’re doing that because they can’t beat VP Sara in a fair election in 2028. That’s why they’re just focusing and using their resources to discredit VP Sara,” Panelo said.
Results of the Sept. 17 to 24 survey released yesterday showed 50 percent of the respondents saying they would vote for Duterte for president if the 2028 elections were held during the survey period.
She had a 24-point margin over Naga City Mayor and former vice president Leni Robredo, who placed second with the support of 26 percent of the respondents.

Next were Sen. Raffy Tulfo with 12 percent, Sen. Risa Hontiveros with three percent, Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro with one percent, Public Works and Highways Secretary Vince Dizon with one percent and Baguio City Mayor Benjie Magalong with 0.3 percent.

articles.title: BOC chief vows no let-up in drive vs agricultural smuggling
articles.summary: Operations against agricultural smuggling will not weaken, Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno assured the public yesterday.

blocks.text: October 14, 2026 | 12:00am

At a Senate hearing, Sen. Francis Pangilinan praised the Bureau of Customs, Department of Agriculture (DA) and Philippine Navy for intercepting two cargo vessels carrying around 20,000 metric tons of rice from Vietnam, with an estimated value of P700 million.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Operations against agricultural smuggling will not weaken, Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno assured the public yesterday.

“We will not allow smugglers to take advantage of our ports for their illegal activities while our farmers are affected. This involves a sizable sum and all the more that we would strengthen our monitoring and cooperation with the DA and other agencies,” Nepomuceno said.
Questionable documents and canceled sanitary and phytosanitary permits had led to the shipments’ seizure.
Authorities intercepted M/V Tay Son 2 on Sept. 17 and MV Lucky Star on Sept. 21.
Tay Son 2 carried 12,500 MT of rice, while Lucky Star had 7,500 MT.
Based on the initial investigation, Pangilinan said it was possible there was a violation of the Anti-Agricultural Economic Sabotage Act of 2024.

articles.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
articles.summary: Sir Ken McCallum says operations to tackle terrorism and state threats are now roughly of an "equal scale".

blocks.text: MI5 is devoting more resource to countering state threats than during the Cold War, the head of the intelligence service has said.

Sir Ken McCallum said threats from foreign adversaries had quadrupled in the last decade, with Russia "aggressor number one" as well as increased Iran-linked aggression against Jewish sites and military bases.
At an annual speech in London, MI5's chief said Russia was waging hybrid warfare at a time when AI was "supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders".
He also warned of rising threats from "extreme right-wing terrorism" and said MI5 had "caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al," including by integrating the technology with drones.
He said the biggest threat from the misuse of AI was extremist groups using the technology to harness new and existing bioweapons.
However, he noted that work countering terrorism and state threats was now "pretty much of equal scale" which he described as a "huge shift" in recent years.

Sir Ken said Russia had stopped short of "conventional conflict" against Nato and is instead trying to unsettle European countries while its progress in its full-scale invasion of Ukraine is "minimal and horrifically costly".

Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyber-attacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary.
These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary.
Sir Ken said MI5 successes in identifying and expelling Russian spies from the UK had left the Kremlin dependent on paying proxies for attempted attacks.
"With its traditional covert footprint eviscerated by almost 1,000 expulsions since the invasion, the Kremlin's global toolkit is weak, he said.
"So we see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding."
He added: "These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand."
His comments come as a growing number of leaders across Europe have warned Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.

Asked after the speech about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's recent comments that Russia interfered with the Brexit referendum, Sir Ken said it was "not new news" that there had been attempts from Moscow but distinguished between "interference attempted" and "outcome achieved".

He said it was a matter of public record that there were pieces in Russian media and "so-called internet trolls and bot farms" seeking to influence the Brexit debate, but also stressed that the result of the 2016 referendum was "not in dispute".
He added that he was "worried" about the the ongoing debate on Russian interference.
"I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall," he told reporters.
Meanwhile, Sir Ken warned that Iran is also expanding a hybrid campaign in the UK.
The intelligence chief said there had been 50 arrests in the last year over Iran-linked activities.
Much of this Iranian aggression has been aimed at Jewish communities, Sir Ken added, and also at "harder targets, like military sites".
Sir Ken did not mention arrests at RAF Fairford directly during his speech, but told reporters afterwards the incident was "not unique".
He added: "We have seen Iranian interest beyond RAF Fairford in the UK."
The incident at the airbase in Gloucesteshire, where three suspicious vans were seen parked nearby, has seen seven people arrested and bailed by counter-terrorism police.
Burnham has said the incident was "almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard".

The MI5 head said in his speech: "What I can say is that those who seek to cause mayhem on British streets - whether hired thugs here or their paymasters overseas - will meet an unflinching response."

Sir Ken added that the National Security Act - a 2023 law designed to target people working against UK interests for foreign powers - is in heavy use, and has been employed to tackle threats from China as well as Iran and Russia.
On the emerging threat posed by AI, Sir Ken said: "It can produce propaganda and radicalising material tailored to the individual.
"We've caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al to improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies, with Al-enabled drones adding a new twist."
Sir Ken said the bioweapons threat posed by AI was "not yet realised" but warned the technology has the "potential to change the stakes".
"These risks are real. The UK Intelligence Community - MI5, GCHQ, MI6 - is working closely with the UK's globally respected AI Security Institute to take them on."
Sir Ken said AI poses unknown threats, telling Thames House: "Put at its simplest, human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are".
He announced MI5 had launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre, which he said would assess sources and "separate the bluster from the realities".
In April, the UK's terrorism threat level was raised to severe for the first time in five years, meaning an attack is highly likely.

Sir Ken said Islamist groups like Al Qaeda and so-called Islamic State both continue to direct and inspire attacks, while the increased risk was also driven "in significant part" by extreme right-wing terrorism.
He continued: "Over the last year the most marked trend has been an increase in cases where extremist versions of anti-immigration and anti-Muslim grievance are tipping into terrorist intent."

Sir Ken said extreme right-wing terrorism tended to "skew young", driven by the internet - adding that MI5 had in recent months investigated a "radicalised extreme right-wing 13-year-old here in the UK".
He said: "That investigation generated insight that enabled one of our international partners to prevent a lethal attack on their soil."

articles.title: DR Congo: Kabila’s move towards M23 raises questions over peace
articles.summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say it could reshape opposition to President…

image.caption: Eyeing a political comeback? Former DRC President Joseph Kabila is a fierce critic of President Felix TshisekediImage: Jospin Mwisha/AFP

blocks.text: Joseph Kabila's decision to lead a new political-military movement, the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), puts the former president of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in more direct confrontation with President Felix Tshisekedi's government. Kabila announced the FRN on October 12 in Goma, eastern DRC, at his residence, where leaders of the AFC/M23 rebel movements joined him.

FRN coalition adviser, Claude Ibalanky, said the group would unite opposition forces, including figures associated with the AFC/M23 movement. The new structure succeeds the Congo River Alliance (AFC), which had been allied with the M23 rebellion. Its leadership includes former AFC leader Corneille Nangaa and M23 political leader Bertrand Bisimwa. Sultani Makenga, a senior M23 military commander, was also assigned a senior role in the new organization.
The announcement comes as diplomatic initiatives seek to end fighting between Congolese government forces and the rebellion.

Congolese authorities have accused Kabila of supporting the insurgency, allegations he has denied. On September 30, 2025, a military court sentenced him to death in absentia after convicting him of treason, war crimes and other offenses linked to the conflict in eastern DRC. Kabila has rejected the case as politically motivated.
Adolph Amisi Makutano, an official of the ruling Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), criticized the former president for taking a more public role.
"It was a lack of courage that made this gentleman drag his feet. They held several meetings and today he is being pushed to step out into the open. But it is a disgrace for the DRC," Makutano said.
Why is eastern Congo at war?
Eastern DRC has experienced decades of conflict involving armed groups, competition over territory andmineral resources, and tensions with neighboring countries.

The aftermath of Rwanda's 1994 genocide against the Tutsicontributed to successive regional conflicts, as armed groups and refugees crossed borders and neighboring states became involved in Congo's civil wars.
7 reasons why eastern DR Congo remains stuck in conflict
M23 takes its name from a March 23, 2009, peace agreement. The movement says the Congolese government failed to honor commitments to integrate its fighters and protect minority Congolese Tutsis.

Kinshasa, the United Nations (UN) and Western governments haveaccused Rwanda of supporting M23 and exercising influence over its operations. Rwanda denies backing the rebellion and cites security threats posed by armed groups operating in Congo. In 2025, M23 captured Goma and Bukavu, two major cities in eastern Congo. Its territorial gains weakened government control across parts of the region, displaced civilians and intensified an already severe humanitarian crisis.
Kabila's leadership of the new front raises questions about whether he intends to consolidate opposition to Tshisekedi, strengthen the rebellion's political leadership, or pursue both.
Political implications of Kabila's move

Alex Vines, Africa program director at the European Council on Foreign Relations, sees the move as evidence that Kabila remains politically ambitious. "It shows Kabila's political ambition is alive and kicking and he is prepared to challenge Tshisekedi," Vines told DW.
Why are tensions rising in the Democratic Republic of Congo?

Timo Roujean, head of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation's office in Kinshasa, cautioned against assessing Kabila's potential support based on ethnic identity alone. He told DW that economic performance and political dynamics in Kabila's home region of Katanga are also relevant.

The new front could give the movement more explicitly political leadership, but it remains unclear whether the reorganization will broaden its domestic support or alter its negotiating position. Conflict analyst Cliffton Chifuwe told DW the alliance does not rule out a negotiated settlement, but could make a durable agreement harder to achieve.
"The Kabila alliance with M23 does not make peace impossible. However, it raises the threshold for achieving that settlement and its ability to hold," Chifuwe told DW.

For Chifuwe, lasting peace requires more than a cessation of hostilities. It also depends on credible security arrangements, the restoration of state authority, humanitarian access, and conditions that allow displaced people to return safely. The new FRN coalition also raises questions for mediators about whether existing peace frameworks can accommodate the political realignment and whether the parties involved can ensure compliance with any agreement.

As this new development plays out, the central issue for civilians in eastern Congo remains whether the leadership change will open a path to settlement or make an already complex conflict harder to resolve.
Wendy Bashi, Saleh Mwanamilongo and Jean Noel Ba Mweze contributed to this article

articles.title: Duane (Keffe D) Davis sentenced to 40 years to life in prison for murder of rapper Tupac Shakur
articles.summary: Duane (Keffe D) Davis received a sentence of to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.

image.caption: Duane Davis, right, and his attorney Michael Sanft are seen in a Las Vegas courtroom in August after a jury found Davis guilty of first-degree murder in the 1996 killing of rapper Tupac Shakur. (Bizuayehu Tesfaye/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·Updated

Duane (Keffe D) Davis received a sentence of to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.
Shakur's siblings spoke during Tuesday's sentencing
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Oct 13, 2026 11:26 AM EDT | Last Updated: 23 minutes ago
Davis was convicted in August of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon. He is the only person ever charged in the death of Shakur, whose popularity was peaking at age 25.
Prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo had said during Tuesday's sentencing that whatever sentence the court imposes, the 63-year-old Davis is "guaranteed to die" behind bars.
The killing went unsolved for years until Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips, gave interviews and published his role in the shooting in his 2019 tell-all memoir.
DiGiacomo said Davis was trying to profit off a killing that he committed, and for that "in my mind, he deserves the maximum possible sentence."
Sekyiwa Shakur and Maurice Shakur, two of the rapper's siblings, spoke during the hearing.

Davis also spoke briefly in court, telling Judge Carli Kierny he wants items back that police took from his house, including his pictures. Asked if there was anything else he wanted to say, Davis said: "No, I'm good."
Davis's lawyer, Michael Sanft, said he plans to appeal the verdict. Sanft said prosecutors waited too long to bring the case.

On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW with music mogul Marion (Suge) Knight when a white Cadillac pulled up at a red light and shots erupted. Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived.

Shakur is considered one of the most influential and versatile rappers of all time and had a burgeoning film career as an actor at the time of his death. His legend has only grown since. His songs still resonate among fans with themes of hardship, love and Black struggles.
Duane Davis found guilty in murder of Tupac Shakur | Hanomansing Tonight

In his memoir, Davis explained how Shakur and his entourage beat up Davis's nephew hours before the shooting in Las Vegas. He said he sought retaliation, and that he was in the passenger seat of the Cadillac and passed the gun to the back seat, where shots were fired. Davis had spoken to detectives years before but avoided prosecution because of an agreement he made with law enforcement.

During the weekslong trial, prosecutors relied on Davis's own statements he made to law enforcement and documentarians. They argued Davis orchestrated the shooting and provided the gun used in Shakur's death, which was the result of a rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru.

Davis's defence attorney pointed to a lack of physical evidence that connected his client to the 30-year-old crime, and he portrayed Davis as a liar who was trying to make money. After nine days of hearing testimony in August, the jury deliberated for three hours before turning over the guilty verdict.
Davis said in court that he plans to appeal.
Rap icon also 'a brother, a son'
Shakur's family is expected to speak at the sentencing, including his siblings Maurice (Mopreme) Shakur and Sekyiwa (Set) Shakur.

Fans of Tupac Shakur hold up a painted portrait of late rapper and actor as they stand with others during a 2023 ceremony honouring him with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in Los Angeles. (Chris Pizzello/Invision/Associated Press)

Following the verdict, prosecutor Binu Palal said that to many people, Shakur was an icon or an idea, "but to the family, Tupac Shakur was a brother, a son, a cousin, a loved person ripped from them 30 years ago."
Palal said the family had to sit through years of Davis "bragging about killing someone they loved."
"They loved that man. And the arrogance that Mr. Davis had in expressing his joy in killing that man ultimately was his undoing," Palal said.

Davis is the only person to be charged and convicted in the killing of Shakur. The three other people who allegedly were in the Cadillac — including Davis's nephew Orlando (Baby Lane) Anderson, who Davis said was the one who pulled the trigger — have died.
'Insufficient evidence' for more charges: prosecutors
Sean (Diddy) Combs and his alleged role were brought up often throughout the trial. Witnesses testified Combs used members of the South Side Compton Crips for security for Bad Boy Records.

In his book and public statements, Davis alleged Combs offered him money to kill Shakur and Knight. Combs, who is serving a four-year prison sentence after being convicted of prostitution-related offences, has repeatedly denied any involvement in the death of Shakur.
Clark County district attorney Steve Wolfson has said his office doesn't believe it has sufficient evidence to charge anyone else.
"But like any other case, if we come into more information, more evidence, we can always consider filing additional charges," he said following the guilty verdict.
"But today, we don't believe that's the appropriate move to make."
